findings.claim: bad front matter crashed the whole listing
an offset generated.at was printed as if it were UTC
the new astimezone(UTC) call raises OverflowError for a datetime at the edge of the range, such as 0001-01-01T00:00:00+01:00, and the command crashes with a traceback
the not-UTF-8 branch of front_matter has no test; only the bad-YAML and non-mapping generated cases are covered

verdict.text: Both round 1 findings are fixed.
One bad handoff is now skipped with a stderr warning naming the file, the rest are still listed, and --json stdout stays one clean list.
Offset timestamps now print in UTC.
Skipping is the right choice over refusing: /continue reads the --json list to resume work, and refusing would block every handoff because of one bad file.
The fixes broke nothing in rows r1 to r4.
Two small non-blocking items remain: an overflow edge case that the astimezone fix added (f3), and an untested branch (f4).
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format and tests pass, rows r1 to r4 pass.
Stamp green: f164bc963fc5e87154d495afed1d24c267bc28b720ef855e9ce873cc499c7bb4.
Read src/kmctl/okf.py, src/kmctl/handoffs.py, the handoffs command in src/kmctl/__init__.py and tests/test_handoffs.py in full.
f1: test_handoffs_skip_bad_front_matter_with_a_warning parses result.stdout as JSON while the warning goes to stderr.
It asserts the good and odd handoffs are listed, and that broken.md is named on stderr.
By hand: a Latin-1 file was skipped with "not UTF-8 text" on stderr, stdout stayed valid JSON, and the exit code was 0.
f2: test_handoffs_dates_are_converted_to_utc checks that +02:00 09:00 prints as 07:00Z.
Ordering is unchanged, because aware datetimes already compared correctly.
By hand: generated.at "0001-01-01T00:00:00+01:00" crashes with OverflowError from astimezone (f3).
f1: resolved.
front_matter raises BadFrontMatter for bad YAML and for non-UTF-8 text.
live_handoffs catches it, appends a warning and continues, and reads generated.at only when generated is a dict (src/kmctl/handoffs.py:52-60).
The command prints each warning to stderr before the output.
f2: resolved.
as_datetime converts aware values with astimezone(UTC) (src/kmctl/okf.py:43), and a test covers it.
f3: open, hardening, non-blocking.
The astimezone call added for f2 overflows near datetime.min or datetime.max.
This is the same class of crash as f1, but only a contrived timestamp triggers it.
A plain fix is enough: catch OverflowError in as_datetime and return None, so the value counts as unreadable.
It does not need my second look.
f4: open, test-strength, non-blocking.
Add a test that writes non-UTF-8 bytes and asserts the file is skipped with a warning.
The code already works, as my probe showed, so the test only guards against regressions and does not need review again.
